message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on novelty pillow-like items containing stuffed figurines. The likely classification is as a stuffed toy, or as a cushion.

Cushions are in 9404.90 (other articles of bedding, stuffed). Toys representing animals or non-human creatures are in 9503.00.0090 (stuffed toys). The figurines are shaped like candy characters, and the Sour Patch Kids are human-like characters, so they would be toys representing humans, which fall under 9503.00.00 other toys. The M&M's are also characters.

I think CBP would classify the set as a composite or set under GRI 3(b). The essential character is the pillow-like bag, which may be a novelty cushion under 9404.90.8580 (other, of man-made fibers, stuffed). Alternatively, it may be treated as a toy, since the item is novelty and play-oriented with removable figurines to play with.

I recall the ruling being N-series, "The applicable subheading for the SOUR PATCH KIDS and M&M's pillow-like items will be 9404.90.8040" or 9503.00.0073? Cushions of "pillow-like" with figurines... I lean toward 9404.90.8580, a tariff number that covers pillows and cushions of other textile materials. The 9404.90.85 line is "Other: Other", and its statistical suffixes are 8505 (pillows and cushions, other) and 8580. I'll go with 9404.90.8580.
